learn.hook: Clink, clink! Glass bangles shine at weddings and festivals. But how does hard glass become a round, sparkly bangle?
points: Firozabad, a city in Uttar Pradesh, is famous for its glass bangles.
Glass is melted in a very hot furnace until it becomes soft.
The soft glass is shaped into coils, cut into rings and joined with heat.
Then the bangles are polished, painted or decorated.
Many skilled people work on each bangle, step by step.

example.q: Read: Zoya's family makes glass bangles in Firozabad. Glass is melted in a very hot furnace, so Zoya watches from a safe distance. Her uncle shapes the soft, glowing glass into long coils. The coils are cut into rings, and the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame. Then Zoya's mother paints tiny flowers on them. 'Each bangle carries the work of many hands,' she says proudly. What happens to the glass after it is shaped into coils?
steps: Find the line about coils: 'The coils are cut into rings'.
Then: 'the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame'.
example.answer: The coils are cut into rings, and the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame.

learn.reallife: When you see a box of shiny bangles at a fair, remember: many artisans worked with great care and skill to make them.

games.title: True or false? (from the story)
items: Zoya's family makes bangles in Firozabad.
The first line says so.

Zoya's uncle shapes the glass into coils.
Her uncle shapes the soft, glowing glass into long coils.
Zoya's mother paints tiny flowers on the bangles.
That is the last step in the story.
The bangles are made of clay in the story.
They are glass bangles.

quiz.q: Read: 'Zoya's family makes glass bangles in Firozabad.' Where does Zoya's family make bangles?
quiz.explain: The line names Firozabad, a city famous for glass bangles.
quiz.mistake: Picks another city without reading the line

quiz.q: Read: 'Glass is melted in a very hot furnace. Her uncle shapes the soft, glowing glass into long coils. The coils are cut into rings.' What is done to the glass first?
options: It is melted in a very hot furnace
It is joined with a flame
quiz.explain: The glass must be melted and made soft before it can be shaped.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the steps

quiz.q: Read: 'Her uncle shapes the soft, glowing glass into long coils.' What shape does the glass take first?
quiz.explain: The uncle shapes the glass into long coils.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the line about shaping

quiz.q: Read: 'The ends of each ring are joined with a small flame.' How are the ends of each ring joined?
quiz.explain: Heat softens the glass so the ends can join.
quiz.mistake: Thinks glass is joined like paper or cloth

quiz.q: Read: 'Then Zoya's mother paints tiny flowers on them.' What does Zoya's mother do?
options: She paints tiny flowers on the bangles
quiz.explain: The line says she paints tiny flowers on them.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up who does which step

quiz.q: Read: ''Each bangle carries the work of many hands,' she says proudly.' What does she mean?
options: Many people work to make one bangle
Bangles are worn on many hands at once
Bangles are made by machines only
quiz.explain: Each step is done by a skilled person, so many people help make each bangle.
quiz.mistake: Takes the words 'many hands' literally

quiz.q: Read: 'Glass is melted in a very hot furnace, so Zoya watches from a safe distance.' Why does Zoya stay away?
quiz.explain: A furnace hot enough to melt glass is dangerous, so children stay at a safe distance.
quiz.mistake: Misses the reason word 'so'

quiz.q: Firozabad, the city of glass bangles, is in which state?
quiz.explain: Firozabad is in Uttar Pradesh. It is famous for glass bangles.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without knowing the fact

teach.ask: Gappu sees a shiny bangle: 'Is it a giant ring for me? How is a glass bangle made?'
teach.praise: Clink, clink! What a clear explanation of a sparkly craft!
teach.nudge: What happens first to the glass? What comes after it is shaped?

learn.hook: A potter turns mud into pots. A weaver turns thread into cloth. Artisans have magic in their hands!
points: An artisan is a skilled worker who makes things by hand.
A potter makes pots from clay. A weaver makes cloth. A carpenter works with wood.
A blacksmith makes tools from iron. A goldsmith makes jewellery from gold.
India has many famous crafts: Madhubani paintings from Bihar, wooden toys from Channapatna in Karnataka, blue pottery from Jaipur.
Handmade things take skill, time and patience, so we should value them.

example.q: Fill in: 'A ___ shapes wet clay on a wheel to make diyas and pots.'
steps: A person who makes pots is a potter.

learn.reallife: At Diwali, we light clay diyas made by potters. At a crafts fair, you may see weavers, painters and toy makers at work.

items.text: A ___ weaves cloth on a loom.

quiz.q: What is an artisan?
options: A person who only sells things
A skilled worker who makes things by hand
A person who drives a bus
quiz.explain: Artisans use skill and their hands to make useful and beautiful things.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word 'artisan'

quiz.q: A potter works with ___.
quiz.explain: Potters shape clay into pots, diyas and cups.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the materials of different artisans

quiz.q: What does a weaver make?
quiz.explain: A weaver weaves threads together on a loom to make cloth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the work of different artisans

quiz.q: A blacksmith works with ___.
quiz.explain: A blacksmith heats and hammers iron to make tools.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a blacksmith with a goldsmith or carpenter

quiz.q: What does a goldsmith make?
quiz.explain: A goldsmith makes ornaments from gold.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up goldsmith and blacksmith

quiz.q: Madhubani paintings are a famous art from which state?
quiz.explain: Madhubani painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state without knowing the fact

quiz.q: Channapatna in Karnataka is famous for ___.
quiz.explain: Channapatna is known for its colourful wooden toys.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous crafts of different places

quiz.q: Why should we value handmade things?
options: They are made in a minute
They take skill, time and hard work
quiz.explain: Each handmade item is the result of an artisan's skill and patience.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the work behind a craft

teach.ask: Gappu builds a nest: 'Am I an artisan? Who are artisans and what do they make?'
teach.praise: Yes, I am a nest-making artisan! Thank you for teaching me!
teach.nudge: Who is an artisan? Can you name one and tell me what they make?

learn.hook: One bangle, two bangles... one box, two boxes... one child, many children! Let's learn how words change from one to many.
points: Most nouns add -s to show more than one: bangle-bangles, toy-toys.
Words ending in s, ss, sh, ch or x add -es: bus-buses, glass-glasses, brush-brushes, box-boxes.
Words ending in a consonant + y change y to i and add -es: city-cities, baby-babies.
Many words ending in f or fe change to -ves: knife-knives, leaf-leaves.
Some words change completely or not at all: child-children, woman-women, tooth-teeth, sheep-sheep.

example.q: Make plural: 'The artisan painted one glass and one box.' Change to many.
steps: 'Glass' ends in ss, so add -es: glasses.
'Box' ends in x, so add -es: boxes.
example.answer: The artisan painted many glasses and many boxes.

learn.reallife: At the bangle shop: 'Two dozen bangles, please, in two boxes!' We use plurals every time we shop.

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'glass'?
quiz.explain: 'Glass' ends in ss, so we add -es: glasses.
quiz.mistake: Uses an apostrophe to make a plural

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
quiz.explain: 'Box' ends in x, so we add -es.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in x

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'city'?
quiz.explain: City ends in a consonant + y, so change y to i and add -es.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the 'y'

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'toy'?
quiz.explain: 'Toy' ends in a vowel + y, so we just add -s.
quiz.mistake: Changes y to i after a vowel

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'knife'?
quiz.explain: 'Knife' changes f to v and adds -es: knives.
quiz.mistake: Just adds -s to a word ending in fe

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
quiz.explain: 'Child' changes completely: children. It already means many, so never add another -s.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to an irregular noun

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'sheep'?
quiz.explain: 'Sheep' stays the same: one sheep, ten sheep.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to every noun

quiz.q: Which sentence uses the plural correctly?
options: The womans are painting the bangles.
The women are painting the bangles.
The womens are painting the bangles.
The woman are painting the bangles.
quiz.explain: The plural of 'woman' is 'women', and it goes with 'are'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to an irregular plural

teach.ask: Gappu counts: 'One leaf, two leafs? One child, two childs? How do I make plurals?'
teach.praise: Two leaves, three children, many thanks! You are the best!
teach.nudge: How do we change a word to mean more than one? What about words like child or leaf?
